```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Create a task, fit a DR-learner, and predict conditional average treatment
effects. The example uses simulated data and simple mean learners, with
cross-fitting and model selection disabled.

```{r}
library(hte3)
library(sl3)

data <- hte3_example_data(n = 120, seed = 1)

task <- hte_task(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y",
  propensity_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  outcome_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  mean_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

model <- fit_cate(
  task,
  method = "dr",
  base_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_validate = FALSE
)

head(predict(model, data))
summary(model)
```

## Cross-fitting and model selection

Use these arguments to control nuisance estimation and model selection:

- `cross_fit` in `hte_task()` controls nuisance estimation.
- `cross_validate` in `fit_cate()` or `fit_crr()` controls selection across
  candidate HTE learners.

Set `cross_fit = TRUE` to estimate each observation's nuisance values using
other folds. Set `cross_validate = TRUE` to compare candidate HTE learners.
